scope: All wrong-owner and mistaken-withdrawal inputs in the completed repair-v2 study; no fresh model generation or training.

method.manual_review: Per-input raw arrived conversation, actual prior state/history, compiled correction and amended reference, and each arm’s actual proposal, recorded runtime result, candidate state, and sealed target judgment.
method.blinding: Retrospective and unblinded; arm identities and frozen score labels were visible.
method.score_policy: Original labels and artifacts preserved. Attribution is separate from frozen scoring.
method.raw_proposal_integrity: 75/75 original output rows match the mapping’s canonical hashes; 75/75 raw JSON operation lists match the reviewed proposals.
method.runtime_execution: No runtime replay by this review; recorded results inspected. The separate runtime audit must substantiate executable-patch claims.

findings: No owner-field correction is proposed in any of the 60 wrong-owner assignments. All 60 retain the faulty supplied owner. The visible error boundary is the proposal, not only state application.

Adapter-disabled touches the target in 12/20 owner inputs: 10 text rewrites without owner repair and 2 mistaken withdrawals. Both LoRA arms leave all 20 owner targets untouched. Seven base target operations cite the original ownership evidence while still omitting the owner field; six preserve equivalent target meaning and one adds a wrong restriction.

For mistaken withdrawal, adapter-disabled and v1 each produce the correct target state in 2/5 inputs; v2 produces it in 0/5. All four successful state reopenings have insufficient target-operation citations under the frozen judgments. This conjunction is a post-hoc diagnostic and does not replace the frozen state-repair score.

One base wrong-withdrawal proposal attempts reopen with an illegal text field and uncertain status. Runtime rejects it. Removing the illegal field alone would still leave the requested active task incorrectly uncertain; runtime-only attribution would therefore be incomplete.
One base owner-cohort patch is rejected for changing an unknown intention. Its proposal never requests owner repair, making the runtime rejection incidental to the missing owner correction.

In three v2 mistaken-withdrawal assignments, other operations explicitly cite the original active-task event but omit reopening. Together with owner evidence citations, this rules out a blanket claim that repair evidence was absent from the supplied input or all emitted citations.

All 25 target repairs can be supported by already-arrived raw evidence. The supplied state histories themselves contain the seeded owner/status error. No target-reference defect or actual raw cancellation was found in this cohort.

representative_source_quotes_without_ass.quote: My reference cross-sections must keep their horizontal scale unchanged.
representative_source_quotes_without_ass.observation: The raw first-person speaker identifies ownership. The supplied target text names that person while both current and historical owner fields name another participant.

This accepts registration ticks outside an image. The full earlier conversation still contains the proof request and never cancels it; the latest feature acceptance does not justify preserving a withdrawn task.
A supplied history entry treats this acknowledgment as a withdrawal even though the raw conversation contains no cancellation.

interpretation: Retention of explicitly contradictory supplied fields is consistent with prior-state anchoring or a latest-event-only update strategy. These are hypotheses, not demonstrated attention, reasoning, or training mechanisms. Citing an event does not establish what the model internally understood.
limitations: Synthetic short dialogues and deliberately corrupted prior states; these are not naturally occurring model-rollout errors.
All repair evidence lies at or before the processed cursor, so this cohort tests historical correction, not only extraction of new turns.
One retrospective model-assisted reviewer; no new independent human adjudication.
Source-field sufficiency and full-state quality are different outcomes; frozen target repair counts alone do not imply evidence-complete or globally correct patches.
Other candidate errors are retained in private frozen judgments but this attribution is scoped to designated owner/withdrawal targets.
No causal intervention, new inference, retraining, production trial, or new improvement estimate.
No runtime acceptability claim is inferred solely from semantic support; use the separate recorded-replay and compiled-patch audit.

private_audit_record.publication_policy: PRIVATE: includes exact case IDs, blinded IDs, per-assignment arm joins, source quotes, raw proposals and frozen judgments; do not publish this record or the input packet.
